_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with chronic or accelerated phase CML with resistance and/or intolerance to two or more tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKI); indication based upon response rate

pivotal_trials.trial_name: CGX-635-CML-202 (CML-202) — pooled with CML-203 into analysis CML-300
pivotal_trials.design: International multicenter, open-label, single-arm trial of subcutaneous omacetaxine in adult CML patients
pivotal_trials.population: Adult CML-CP and CML-AP patients who received 2 or more approved TKIs with documented resistance or intolerance to dasatinib and/or nilotinib (pooled subset analysis CML-300)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: MCyR (major cytogenetic response) for CP CML; MaHR (major hematologic response = CHR or NEL) for AP CML
pivotal_trials.n: CP CML efficacy population N=76; AP CML efficacy population N=35
pivotal_trials.result: CP CML: MCyR 14 (18.4%) (95% CI 10.5%–29.0%), median MCyR duration 12.5 months. AP CML: MaHR 5 (14.3%) (95% CI 4.5%–30.3%), median MaHR duration 4.7 months

nct_ctgov.title: Homoharringtonine (Omacetaxine Mepesuccinate) in Treating Patients With Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML) With the T315I BCR-ABL Gene Mutation

pivotal_trials.trial_name: CGX-635-CML-203 (CML-203) — pooled with CML-202 into analysis CML-300
pivotal_trials.design: International multicenter, open-label, single-arm trial of subcutaneous omacetaxine in adult CML patients
pivotal_trials.population: Adult CML patients who failed or were intolerant to prior TKI therapy; contributed resistant/intolerant CP and AP patients to pooled analysis CML-300
pivotal_trials.endpoint: MCyR for CP CML; MaHR (CHR or NEL) for AP CML (endpoints assessed in pooled analysis CML-300)
pivotal_trials.n: CML-203 enrolled n=100 (pooled into analysis CML-300)
pivotal_trials.result: Pooled efficacy (analysis CML-300): CP CML MCyR 18.4%; AP CML MaHR 14.3%

nct_ctgov.title: Open Label Study of Subcutaneous Homoharringtonine (Omacetaxine Mepesuccinate) in Patients With Advanced CML

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%): thrombocytopenia, anemia, neutropenia, diarrhea, nausea, fatigue, asthenia, injection site reaction, pyrexia, infection, lymphopenia. Grade 3/4 thrombocytopenia (85% CP, 88% AP), neutropenia (81% CP, 71% AP), anemia (62% CP, 80% AP); fatalities related to myelosuppression in 3% of safety population (N=163)
target_moa: Mechanism not fully elucidated but includes inhibition of protein synthesis, independent of direct Bcr-Abl binding; binds the A-site cleft in the peptidyl-transferase center of the large ribosomal subunit and reduces Bcr-Abl protein levels
modality: Small molecule (cephalotaxine ester; protein synthesis inhibitor), molecular weight 545.6 g/mol

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee convened for this submission; the applicant dropped the T315I indication and the division had approved other CML agents on similar single-arm response data (a prior ODAC for NDA 22374 was held March 22, 2010)

description.text: Fulfilled Subpart H postmarketing requirement (final CGX-635-CML-300 analysis); no change to indication

citations.quote: We approved this NDA under the regulations at 21 CFR 314 Subpart H for accelerated approval of new drugs for serious or life-threatening illnesses. Approval of this supplement fulfills your commitments made under 21 CFR 314.510.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Response rate — major cytogenetic response (MCyR) in CP CML and major hematologic response (MaHR) in AP CML; indication based upon response rate, with no verification of symptom improvement or survival

citations.quote: SYNRIBO for Injection is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with chronic or accelerated phase chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) with resistance and/or intolerance to two or more tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKI). This indication is based upon response rate. There are no trials verifying an improvement in disease-related symptoms or increased survival with SYNRIBO. (1)

confirmatory_requirement.text: Continue follow-up and submit a final analysis report of CGX-635-CML-300 with 24 months minimum follow-up per patient (PMR 1930-1), required under accelerated approval regulations to verify and describe clinical benefit

citations.quote: Products approved under the accelerated approval regulations, 21 CFR 314.510, require further adequate and well-controlled studies/clinical trials to verify and describe clinical benefit. You are required to conduct such studies/trials with due diligence.

1930-1 Continue follow-up of patients (on treatment and in protocol defined post-treatment follow-up) and submit a final analysis report of CGX-635-CML-300 with 24 months of minimum follow-up data for each patient. If 24 months of follow-up is not possible for certain patients, justification should be provided.

orphan_indication.text: Omacetaxine was granted orphan drug designation for treatment of patients with CML on March 10, 2006

citations.quote: Omacetaxine was granted orphan drug designation for treatment of patients with CML in March 10, 2006 exempting it from the requirements of the Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA).

summary.text: Synribo received accelerated approval on the basis of response rate (MCyR in CP CML and MaHR in AP CML) from a post-hoc subset (analysis CML-300) of two single-arm phase 2 trials (CML-202, CML-203), with a required post-marketing confirmatory report of CGX-635-CML-300 with 24-month follow-up; omacetaxine had orphan drug designation for CML. A prior CR letter (April 8, 2010) applied to a separate application (NDA 22374) for the T315I indication, which the applicant forwent.

citations.quote: the recommended regulatory action is accelerated approval of omacetaxine mepesuccinate (subsequently referred to in this review as omacetaxine) as third line therapy for the treatment of accelerated or chronic phase chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML), by subcutaneous route of administration.

The efficacy results from this post-hoc subset analysis of two single-arm trials are adequate given the absence of any approved drug in the third line setting for treatment of CML. This analysis was agreed to by the FDA after the initial application received a CR letter.
Omacetaxine was granted orphan drug designation for treatment of patients with CML in March 10, 2006 exempting it from the requirements of the Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA).

requirement.text: 1930-2: Conduct a Phase 1/2 single-arm trial to investigate the PK, safety, and preliminary efficacy of omacetaxine following fixed dose administration in CP or AP CML patients who have failed two or more TKI therapies

requirement.text: 1930-3: Conduct a mass balance trial in humans to determine the disposition and elimination pathways and characterize the major metabolites of omacetaxine following subcutaneous injection

citations.quote: 1930-3 Conduct a mass balance trial in humans to determine the disposition and elimination pathways as well as to characterize the major metabolites of omacetaxine following subcutaneous injection. Depending on the results, hepatic and/or renal impairment trials may be required.
